newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City eco-train works to start in May -paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City eco-train works to start in May -paper.

text.p: Work on Mexico City's long-awaited, elevated eco-train project is scheduled to start in May, the national daily Reforma said Tuesday.

Delays in the start-up of the project have forced up costs for the construction of the train by 50 percent to $1.124 billion from $750 million, Reforma said, citing Ariel Aguirre, the director of public transport in the capital.

Opposition to the train's intended route, which will wend its way from the city centre to northern outskirts, have been behind the delays in the project, which was awarded by the city government to a consortium back in November 1994.
The concession to build and operate the train for 18 years was given to Grupo Mexico de Desarrollo, Grupo Riobo, Grupo Tribasa, Canada's Bombardier Inc. and Concarril.
Reforma said official estimates have construction lasting 36 months, with works only ongoing at night to avoid traffic problems.
